deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to a draft proof of the basic properties of the Schatten classes L^p(H), 0<p≤∞, with S_p(A)=Σ s_i(A)^p and ||A||_p = S_p(A)^{1/p}. The task is to show that ||·||_p is a norm for p≥1 and that S_p is subadditive (a p-norm) for 0<p<1.

(i) Duality for 1≤p≤∞. The previous page proved |Tr(AB)| ≤ ||A||_p whenever ||B||_{p'}≤1, using the Hölder-type formula (6). This page shows the bound is sharp.
- Polar decomposition gives a partial isometry U with UA=|A|.
- Diagonalize |A| and apply classical Hölder duality between l^p and l^{p'} to the eigenvalue sequence. This gives H in L^{p'} with ||H||_{p'}≤1 and Tr(H|A|)=||A||_p, for instance H=|A|^{p-1}/||A||_p^{p-1}. For p=∞ one only gets this approximately, by finite-rank H.
- Then Tr(HUA)=||A||_p. Put B=HU. The ideal inequality (5) gives ||B||_{p'} ≤ ||U||·||H||_{p'} ≤ 1.
- Hence (7): ||A||_p = sup_{||B||_{p'}≤1} |Tr AB|. So ||A||_p is a supremum of seminorms A ↦ |Tr AB| and is therefore a seminorm, which gives the triangle inequality.

(ii) For 0<p<1 duality fails, so he switches to an analytic route. Lemma 1: let α_i≥0, 0<p<1 and f(z)=Π(1+α_i z). Then (8): Σ α_i^p = (p sin πp/π) ∫_0^∞ log f(x) x^{-1-p} dx, both sides possibly infinite.
- Proof: by Tonelli it reduces to one factor. The substitution u=αx gives ∫_0^∞ log(1+αx)x^{-1-p}dx = α^p ∫_0^∞ log(1+u)u^{-1-p}du.
- Integrating by parts, this equals (α^p/p)∫_0^∞ u^{-p}/(1+u) du = α^p π/(p sin πp).

The next page applies (8) to f(z)=det(1+z|A|), where M(r)=f(r). He then uses the determinant inequality det(1+r|A+B|) ≤ det(1+r|A|)det(1+r|B|) to get S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for 0<p<1. This is the 'formula (4)' being proved. The method is the Rotfel'd/Seiler–Simon route: an integral representation of x^p through log(1+tx), plus a Fredholm-determinant inequality.
errors: The phrase read as 'dimension finie' for H is doubtful. For 1<p<∞ the extremal H=|A|^{p-1}/||A||_p^{p-1} has finite rank only if A does. For p=∞ (p'=1) the supremum in (7) is generally not attained. Finite rank only works approximately, which is harmless since (7) is a sup.

Lemma 1 implicitly needs the product to converge, i.e. Σα_i<∞, or else the convention log f=+∞. With α_i≥0, Tonelli justifies 'both sides may be infinite'. The struck-out hypothesis was correctly dropped.
On the next page, M_A(r)=sup_{|z|=r} det(1+zA) should be sup |det(1+zA)|. The determinant inequality (10) is cited with an illegible reference and is not proved on these pages.
Formula (5) is invoked here as a simple ideal inequality. Yet the next page says he knows only a 'complicated method' for (5). This suggests the numbering of the formulas was still in flux.

ideas.what: Duality ||A||_p = sup_{||B||_{p'}≤1}|Tr AB| via polar decomposition plus Hölder on singular values, giving the triangle inequality for Schatten norms p≥1
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (1955) or in Produits tensoriels topologiques; unsure

ideas.what: Integral representation Σα_i^p = (p sin πp/π)∫_0^∞ log Π(1+α_i x) x^{-1-p} dx, i.e. x^p as a positive superposition of log(1+tx)
ideas.modern_name: Integral representation of operator-concave power functions / Rotfel'd trick
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lindelöf/Valiron-type formulas for canonical products); used for trace inequalities by Rotfel'd (1968–69) and by Seiler–Simon (1975), Simon's 'Trace Ideals'
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956), on the growth of det(1+zA) and Schatten classes; unsure

ideas.what: Proof of the p-triangle inequality S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for 0<p<1 via the log-determinant inequality det(1+|A+B|) ≤ det(1+|A|)det(1+|B|) and (8)
ideas.modern_name: Rotfel'd / McCarthy inequality for Schatten quasi-norms; Seiler–Simon determinant inequality

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck proves the subadditivity of S_p for 0<p<1 on Schatten classes. He uses exactly the method later published by Seiler and Simon (1975) and presented in Simon's 'Trace Ideals': write x^p as (p sin πp/π)∫ log(1+tx)t^{-1-p}dt and combine it with det(1+t|A+B|) ≤ det(1+t|A|)det(1+t|B|). The result itself is usually credited to McCarthy/Rotfel'd (1967–69).
missed.quote: Une telle démonstration n'est plus utilisable pour p<1; nous démontrerons la formule (4), par voie analytique, grâce au Lemme 1 ... (8) Σ α_i^p = (p sin πp/π) ∫_0^∞ log f(x)/x^{1+p} dx
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would push back by about 15–20 years both the p<1 triangle inequality for Schatten classes and the determinant/integral-representation proof technique. It would credit Grothendieck in the history of trace-ideal inequalities, unless it already appears in his 1955 Bourbaki exposé or his 1956 Fredholm paper (to be checked).

missed.claim: The page links Schatten-class quasi-norms to the growth function M(r) of the Fredholm determinant det(1+zA), via a Lindelöf-type integral (formula (9) on the next page). This is an exact identity S_p(A) = c_p∫ log M_{|A|}(r) r^{-1-p}dr, bridging entire-function theory and operator ideals.
missed.quote: (9) S_p(A) = p (sin πp/π) ∫_0^∞ log M_{|A|}(r)/r^{1+p} dr
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly classical in spirit, but its explicit use as a tool for convexity inequalities in operator ideals predates the literature that usually credits it.

deep.surprise_reason: The duality argument is routine. The p<1 subadditivity proof via the integral representation and a Fredholm-determinant inequality, however, anticipates McCarthy/Rotfel'd (1967–69) and especially the Seiler–Simon (1975) method by many years. It may have partially surfaced in Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki exposé or his Fredholm paper, which I cannot confirm, so I stay at 5.
transcription_corrections: 'on peut trouver [?] dimension [?] finie [?] H ∈ L^{p'}' is uncertain; the image suggests 'on peut trouver ... H ∈ L^{p'} tel que Tr(H|A|) = ||A||_p'. Any 'finie' should be read as an approximation, not a literal claim.

In the image the left side of the assertion following 'soit' is enclosed in brace-like delimiters (rendered '{Tr(HUA)}', probably absolute-value bars or emphasis); the transcription gives it simply as 'Tr(HUA) = ||A||_p'. The identity itself is correct.
'grâce au' is correct; Lemme 1 has a marginal 'et soit' insertion before '0<p<1', consistent with the transcription.
Next page: M_A(r) should read sup_{|z|=r} |det(1+zA)|, with absolute value.
